builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Folio: Recoverable Multi-Resolution Context Folding for Long-Horizon Language Agents
summary: Folio replaces model-written summarization-based context compaction with a programmatic fold over three pre-existing linked views (model-written turn notes, a runtime event manifest, and full source records), printing handles so bounded recovery tools can re-read evidence on demand. It adds per-reply turn-note generation and persistent storage of event manifests and source records, plus recovery tooling and a dossier, but removes the inference cost and latency of each compaction pass (median fold 0.6 s). It can fail when turn notes omit details later needed, when handle-based retrieval returns the wrong evidence, or when the fold trigger's landing-point pricing misfires on workloads with irregular token growth.
rationale: The gains are reported on a single benchmark with one backend model and depend on runtime instrumentation and recovery tools, so the approach is plausible and low-cost to adopt but requires validation on the reader's own agent workloads before production use.
technique: Programmatic multi-level context folding with recoverable handles

claims.statement: Folio replaces model-written summarization-based context compaction with a programmatic fold over three pre-existing linked views (model-written turn notes, a runtime event manifest, and full source records), printing handles so bounded recovery tools can re-read evidence on demand. It adds per-reply turn-note generation and persistent storage of event manifests and source records, plus recovery tooling and a dossier, but removes the inference cost and latency of each compaction pass (median fold 0.6 s). It can fail when turn notes omit details later needed, when handle-based retrieval returns the wrong evidence, or when the fold trigger's landing-point pricing misfires on workloads with irregular token growth.

On 75 LOCA-bench tasks with DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Folio solves 66 tasks versus 54 for the same runtime with model-written compaction, at 2.4x lower cost and about half the working time, with a median fold time of 0.6 seconds.
